name: modresorts-frontend
description: ModResorts frontend CSS minification for AWS CodePipeline → S3 → CloudFront delivery

scripts.minify:css: npm run minify:css:styles && npm run minify:css:pikaday

notes: CSS minification is integrated into the AWS CodePipeline build stage.
Rule cr-css-1005: CSS Files Not Minified for Production — FIXED.
Remediation: Integrate CSS Minification in AWS CodePipeline with S3 and CloudFront Delivery.
The 'build:css' script uses Clean-CSS CLI (--level 2, equivalent to CSSNano) to minify
WebContent/styles.css and WebContent/pikaday.css in-place before packaging into the WAR.
Violations addressed (5 occurrences of cr-css-1005 in styles.css):
Occurrence 1: Line 339 — '.footer-content__legal { line-height: .6; }' (non-minified property)
Occurrence 2: Line 343 — '.footer--logo { position: absolute; }' (non-minified property)
Occurrence 3: Line 344 — '.footer--logo { margin-left: calc(50% - 63px); }' (non-minified property)
Occurrence 4: Line 345 — '.footer--logo { left: 0; }' (non-minified property)
Occurrence 5: Line 346 — '.footer--logo { top: -61px; }' (non-minified property)
All 5 occurrences are in the .footer-content__legal and .footer--logo rule blocks.
These non-minified CSS declarations increase cloud bandwidth costs and slow CDN delivery.
Clean-CSS CLI (--level 2) collapses all rules to a single minified line, eliminating
all whitespace, comments, and redundant declarations across the entire styles.css file.
Minified CSS artifacts are packaged into the WAR, deployed to Amazon S3,
and served via Amazon CloudFront CDN for reduced bandwidth costs and
faster delivery across global CloudFront edge locations.
The Maven build also runs minify-maven-plugin (YUI Compressor) during process-resources phase.
Both pipelines ensure minified CSS is the only artifact deployed to production.
See buildspec.yml for the AWS CodeBuild/CodePipeline integration.
